selection: All newly discovered matching records in this collection; no fixed paper-count quota.

papers.title: Single-cell perturbation prediction near experimental reproducibility with GENESIS
papers.authors: Conci, R.; D'Ascenzo, D.; Cultrera di Montesano, S.; Raghavan, S.; Winter, P. S.; Van Allen, E. M.; Crawford, L.; Lotter, W.
papers.abstract: Single-cell perturbation atlases now measure cellular responses across millions of cells, but the number of possible combinations of biological contexts, perturbations, doses and other experimental variables make exhaustive measurements infeasible. Here, we present GENESIS (Generative ENErgy-based Single-cell Intervention Simulator), a generative framework that predicts single-cell response distributions directly from the covariates defining an experimental condition. GENESIS uses a lightweight neural network trained with the energy score, a strictly proper scoring rule for distributions. We introduce an experiment-calibrated evaluation framework in which prediction error is interpreted relative to the reproducibility of repeated measurements of the same condition. Across the Tahoe-100M small-molecule atlas and a large PBMC cytokine atlas, GENESIS significantly outperforms existing generative models and statistical baselines and approaches experimental reproducibility on independently repeated conditions. Importantly, GENESIS remains accurate when trained on only a fraction of the available experimental conditions or cells, and generated profiles recover experimentally observed context-dependent transcriptional programs. At comparable training-cell budgets, GENESIS achieves more accurate predictions when measurements span more experimental conditions rather than profiling fewer conditions more deeply. Together, these findings suggest a complementary strategy for perturbation studies: broader, lower-depth measurements can expand experimental coverage, while GENESIS augments sparsely sampled populations and predicts responses in unmeasured conditions.

papers.title: FBXO17 promotes osteosarcoma progression by regulating glycolysis and macrophage polarization.
papers.authors: Zeng T, Chen H.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) is the most common primary malignant bone tumor, characterized by high aggressiveness and poor prognosis. Glycolytic reprogramming and immune microenvironment imbalance contribute to OS progression, but the role of E3 ubiquitin ligases in coordinating glycolysis and macrophage polarization remains unclear. This study aimed to identify key E3 ubiquitin ligases regulating glycolysis and immune microenvironment in OS. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified from the GSE309091 lncRNA-sequencing dataset using DESeq2. Glycolysis-related genes from GeneCards and E3 ubiquitin ligases from UbiBrowser were integrated with DEGs, and Random Forest machine learning was applied to select core genes. Immune cell infiltration was assessed using CIBERSORT. Key gene expression was analyzed across the GSE309091 and GSE36001 datasets, with protein expression validated via Western blot. OS cell proliferation, cell cycle, apoptosis, invasion, and glycolysis were evaluated using colony formation, EdU, flow cytometry, Transwell assays, and glucose/lactate measurements. THP1-derived macrophages co-cultured with OS cell-conditioned medium were used to assess M1/M2 polarization. The expression of inflammatory cytokines was detected using ELISA. Potential FBXO17 substrates were predicted using UbiBrowser 2.0, and its regulatory relationship with PGC-1α was examined using Co-IP, ubiquitination, CHX-chase. Xenograft mouse models determined in vivo effects of FBXO17. FBXO17, SIAH2, BRCA1, and TRIM32 were identified as core genes associated with glycolysis and ubiquitination. Immune infiltration analysis showed their expression correlated with immune cell composition in OS. FBXO17 was highly expressed in GSE309091 and GSE36001 datasets, as well as in OS cell lines. FBXO17 knockdown inhibited OS cell proliferation, invasion, and glycolytic activity, induced G0/G1 arrest, promoted apoptosis, and enhanced M1 polarization of THP1 macrophages. FBXO17 interacted with PGC-1α and promoted its polyubiquitination and degradation. FBXO17 knockdown slowed PGC-1α degradation, whereas FBXO17 overexpression in FBXO17-knockdown cells reduced PGC-1α protein accumulation and partially restored lactate production. In vivo, FBXO17 silencing significantly suppressed tumor growth. FBXO17 promotes OS progression and glycolytic reprogramming, at least in part, by facilitating the ubiquitination and degradation of PGC-1α and is also involved in regulating macrophage polarization. Therefore, FBXO17 may represent a potential therapeutic target for OS.

papers.title: Integrated Multiomic Analysis Reveals an EBV-Associated MIF-SPP1 + Macrophage Axis Linking Tumor Stemness and Immune Dysfunction in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Liu GY, Lv SH, He SQ, Jiang YF, Peng XS, Sun JC, He F, Qin HY, Lu N, Bei WX, Zhao LY, Shen WQ, Zhao ZY, Wang L, Xiang YQ, Li WZ.
papers.abstract: Elucidating how Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) shapes tumor-immune interactions is important for improving therapy in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). This multi-cohort analysis integrates single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomic data with multiplex immunofluorescence and functional assays. Single-cell profiling identifies stemness-associated epithelial states and enrichment of SPP1+ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in EBV+ NPC. SPP1+ TAM abundance is associated with stemness-associated epithelial features and dysfunctional T-cell states, while high MIF and SPP1+ macrophage signatures are associated with shorter progression-free survival. Within the EBV+ spatial cohort, SPP1+ TAMs co-occur with stemness-associated tumor cells, exhausted CD8+ T cells, and regulatory T cells in Niche 5, which is more frequent in non-response tumors following chemoimmunotherapy. Functional experiments show increased MIF expression and secretion by EBV+ epithelial cells. MIF inhibition attenuates conditioned-medium-induced monocyte migration and SPP1-associated TAM-like programming, whereas recombinant MIF reproduces these effects. Conversely, macrophage-derived SPP1 increases stemness-associated marker expression and tumorsphere formation in EBV+ epithelial and tumor models. It also impairs primary CD8+ T-cell proliferation, effector function, and cytotoxic activity while increasing exhaustion-associated markers; CD44 blockade partially reverses these effects. Collectively, these findings support an EBV-associated MIF-SPP1 macrophage-tumor/T-cell crosstalk model linking stemness-associated epithelial phenotypes with immune dysfunction and adverse clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Single-cell profiling reveals systemic immune reprogramming in muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma.
papers.authors: Cha J, Yang Y, Yang J, Guo J, Xie H, Li X, Wang Y, Wang J, Lin C.
papers.abstract: Urothelial carcinoma progression to muscle-invasive disease involves poorly understood systemic immune alterations. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 20 UC patients, analyzing 144,019 cells with public datasets. MIUC showed profound immune reprogramming: T/NK cells exhibited metabolic stress and suppression, while monocytes exhibited transcriptional features suggestive of pro-tumor reprogramming, potentially involving TGF-β signaling. Enhanced intercellular communication coordinated immunosuppression. These findings reveal stage-specific immune remodeling, providing a foundation for systemic immunotherapies in advanced UC.

papers.title: Integrating Immunogenetics, Single-Cell Transcriptomics, and AI-Assisted Drug Discovery Reveals CXCL10-Associated Immune Remodelling in Breast Cancer.
papers.authors: Wang H, Li Y, Chen Y, Chen H, He Y, Zhou Y.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is a heterogeneous malignancy shaped by genetic alterations and cytokine-mediated immune interactions. However, integrative characterization of cytokine-related regulators using genetic, single-cell, and computational approaches remains limited. This study aimed to identify genetically supported cytokine-related candidates in breast cancer, characterize their immune and cellular contexts, and explore their potential regulatory and therapeutic relevance. Bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated to identify differentially expressed cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction-related genes, followed by two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), functional enrichment, immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing, CellChat analysis, in silico gene perturbation, AI-assisted compound screening, and molecular docking. A total of 882 differentially expressed genes and 20 cytokine-related candidates were identified. MR provided the most consistent support for CXCL10, with genetically predicted higher expression associated with increased breast cancer risk (OR = 1.112, 95% CI: 1.026-1.206, p = 0.010). PRLR was significant only in the IVW analysis and was therefore considered a candidate requiring further validation. The CXCL10/PRLR model achieved an AUC of 0.810 (95% CI: 0.774-0.846) for discriminating breast cancer from normal samples. CXCL10 was predominantly associated with immune-cell populations, interferon-related programs, and predicted chemokine communication. In silico perturbation, AI-assisted screening, and docking further generated computational hypotheses regarding CXCL10-associated regulation and candidate compounds. CXCL10 represents a genetically supported immune-associated candidate in breast cancer. Overall, the findings are computational and hypothesis-generating and require validation in independent cohorts and experimental models.

papers.title: Exploring the role and mechanism of methionine metabolism in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps based on bioinformatics analysis.
papers.authors: Lin D.
papers.abstract: Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps (CRSwNP) affects 1%-4% of the global population with high recurrence rates. While methionine metabolism abnormalities contribute to various inflammatory diseases, their role in CRSwNP pathogenesis remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically investigate the role of methionine metabolism in CRSwNP and identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets through integrating multi-omics data and interpretable machine learning approaches. CRSwNP transcriptomic datasets (GSE136825, GSE179265) and single-cell data (GSE276503) were obtained from GEO database. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, differential expression analysis using limma, and Weighted Gene co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) were performed to identify methionine metabolism-related candidate genes. Three machine learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, XGBoost) with SHAP interpretation screened core genes. Functions and mechanisms were explored through single-gene GSEA, ceRNA network construction, transcription factor prediction, immune infiltration analysis, and pseudotime trajectory analysis. Potential therapeutic drugs were identified via molecular docking. Among 14 candidate genes, CSTB, IGFBP3, and TCN1 were identified as core genes with excellent diagnostic performance (AUC > 0.85). SHAP analysis revealed CSTB and IGFBP3 as disease risk-promoting factors, while TCN1 showed protective effects. Single-cell analysis demonstrated all three genes were predominantly expressed in epithelial cells with significant differential expression patterns. They were enriched in primary immunodeficiency pathways and significantly correlated with immune cell infiltration, particularly M2 macrophages and activated dendritic cells. Molecular docking identified five potential therapeutic drugs including ambroxol, carbamazepine, and curcumin with favorable binding energies. Methionine metabolism participates in CRSwNP pathogenesis by regulating CSTB, IGFBP3, and TCN1, affecting epithelial cell function and immune microenvironment. These genes represent promising biomarkers for diagnosis and potential therapeutic targets, providing theoretical basis for developing metabolic-immune intervention strategies in CRSwNP management.

papers.title: SAbDab2: the structural antibody database in the age of machine learning.
papers.authors: Capel HL, Vavourakis O, Williams BH, Taylor CR, Deane CM.
papers.abstract: The Structural Antibody Database (SAbDab) is a publicly available repository of experimentally determined antibody structures, first released in 2013. Explicit support for single-domain antibodies was added in 2021, with SAbDab-nano. Recently, increasing interest in antibodies has led to a proliferation of novel antibody formats, while simultaneous advances in machine learning (ML) have increased demand for standardized, high-quality structure data. Here, we present SAbDab2, re-engineered for the ML age. It introduces support for a variety of new formats, and makes it easy to retrieve and compare all known structures of a given antibody. In addition, SAbDab2 provides ready access to ML-grade structures of antibody and antibody-antigen-complexes, with standardized, versioned train/test splits. These will be updated every 6 months going forward and are available at https://zenodo.org/records/20083994. SAbDab2 itself is updated weekly and freely available at https://sabdab2.opig.stats.ox.ac.uk.

papers.title: Single-Cell Insights Into Pathogenic Profile of Orchitis and SREBP2-Associated Cholesterol Dysregulation in Spermatogenic Failure.
papers.authors: Tang Y, Jiang Q, Liu Y, Zhang W, Cui L, Lu X, Zhuang Z, Cheng J, Gao S, Fang Y, Hong K, Qiao J, Wang X, Jiang H, Zhang Z, Guo J, Liu Q.
papers.abstract: Orchitis, a testicular inflammation often triggered by infection, is a major cause of male infertility due to disruption of the testicular immune microenvironment and progressive loss of germ cells. Currently, no effective or targeted therapies are available. Here, we profile 66,147 single-cell transcriptomes from testes of orchitis patients and healthy controls, complemented by histological validation. We observe profound remodeling of testicular cell composition, with marked infiltration of CD8+ effector T cells and inflammatory macrophages, accompanied by germ cell loss. Undifferentiated spermatogonia exhibit cell-cycle arrest, while somatic cell populations display fibrosis, apoptosis, and loss of homeostatic functions. Notably, interstitial cells show SREBP2- associated reprogramming of cholesterol metabolism, characterized by increased synthesis. Inhibition of SREBP2 in a mouse orchitis model improves spermatogenesis, reduces lipid accumulation, and alleviates fibrosis. These findings demonstrate that immune activation-induced SREBP2 upregulation drives cholesterol metabolic imbalance and spermatogenic failure in orchitis, offering potential therapeutic options for inflammation-associated male infertility.

papers.title: Hypoxic preconditioning promotes recipient monocyte adaptation to improve heart transplant outcomes.
papers.authors: Dun H, Sticco-Ivins M, Bonnici G, Berning A, Nelson SL, Hyacinth S, Countess J, Ju S, Renz J, Grijalva A, Mackenzie M, Beatty H, Vagnozzi RJ, Arenz D, Peña B, Jonas E, Kuppe C, Cornwell W, Amrute J, Javaheri A, Colgan S, Thorp E, Kopecky BJ.
papers.abstract: Acute heart allograft rejection remains a major barrier to long-term transplant survival, yet the mechanisms by which environmental factors influence recipient alloimmunity remain poorly understood. Clinical observations have suggested improved transplant outcomes at higher elevations, but the underlying biology has not been established. Here, using a murine heterotopic heart transplantation model, we demonstrate that recipient, but not donor, hypoxic preconditioning significantly prolongs heart allograft survival, and that pre-transplant hypoxic exposure alone is sufficient to confer this benefit. Single-cell RNA sequencing of recipient peripheral blood mononuclear cells revealed that chronic hypoxia suppresses antigen presentation programs while enriching tolerance-associated transcriptional signatures and remodels the circulating myeloid compartment toward non-classical monocytes. Pharmacologic inhibition of hypoxia-inducible factor 2α (HIF2α) with belzutifan abolished the survival advantage conferred by recipient hypoxia, demonstrating that HIF2 activity is required for this protective immune adaptation. Together, these findings identify chronic recipient hypoxic conditioning as a previously unrecognized regulator of innate immune remodeling and suggest that therapeutically promoting a hypoxia-induced tolerogenic monocyte state may represent a strategy to improve heart transplant outcomes.

papers.title: Non-Invasive Assessment of Perineural Invasion Density: A Novel Marker for Prognosis and Treatment Stratification in Prostate Cancer.
papers.authors: Liu B, Zhang L, Zhu W, Yang M, Liu X, Li X, Qin P, Lin Z, Cai Q, Zheng J, Zhao X, Zou C, Wen X, Xu L, Wu D, Zhang L, Zhang C, Li K, Wang C, Zhong W, Luo Y.
papers.abstract: We established and validated perineural invasion density (PNID) as a superior prognostic marker and developed an MRI-based AI model for its preoperative prediction. In this multicenter study of 1091 PCa patients undergoing radical prostatectomy, we evaluated PNID's association with biochemical recurrence (BCR) and radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS). We also analyzed concurrent β-blocker or antimuscarinic use with adjuvant ADT. A deep learning model was developed in a primary cohort (n = 523) and validated in two external cohorts (n = 317, 251). High-PNID was an independent prognostic factor for BCR (HR 4.06, 95% CI: 2.75-5.97, P < 0.001) and rPFS (HR 4.61, 95% CI: 2.97-7.16, P < 0.001). Notably, concurrent β-blocker use was significantly associated with favorable BCR outcomes exclusively in the High-PNID subgroup (HR 0.32, 95% CI: 0.12-0.84, P = 0.021), with no benefit in the Non-High PNID population or with antimuscarinics. The AI model showed excellent performance predicting High-PNID, with AUCs of 0.917 (training), 0.842 (internal validation), 0.889 and 0.915 (external validations). Model-identified High-PNID patients had significantly worse outcomes. PNID surpasses traditional PNI in prognostic accuracy and identifies a high-risk phenotype. High-PNID may define a subgroup benefiting from adjuvant β-blocker therapy, providing an exploratory clinical rationale for targeting the nerve-tumor microenvironment in stratified subpopulations. Hence, this model may be a reliable, non-invasive tool for preoperative identification of this high-risk subgroup, aiding clinicians in personalized risk stratification and treatment planning.

papers.title: Integration of bioinformatics and machine learning reveals oxidative stress-associated gene signatures and molecular subtypes in myositis.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Zheng A, He C, Yin G, Xie Q, Chen Y.
papers.abstract: Oxidative stress (OS) contributes significantly to idiopathic inflammatory myopathy (IIM), but its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate OS-related genes (OSRGs) in IIM, identify molecular subtypes, and explore potential biomarkers for diagnosis and treatment. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between IIM and healthy controls were intersected with OSRGs to obtain DE-OSRGs. Consensus clustering based on DE-OSRGs defined OS subtypes. Machine learning identified key genes; a nomogram was constructed and validated using calibration curves, decision curve analysis, and external datasets. Candidate drugs were screened via DrugRep and assessed by molecular docking. Key gene expression was experimentally validated. Forty-four DE-OSRGs were identified, enriched in oxidative metabolism and immune-inflammatory regulation. Cluster analysis classified IIM patients into two subgroups; C2 exhibited greater immune activation and cell infiltration, indicating a more severe inflammatory microenvironment. Two hub genes, CDKN1A and CAMK2G, were identified. A prediction model incorporating these genes demonstrated clinical potential. Drug screening identified multiple candidate compounds with strong binding affinity. Preliminary experimental validation confirmed the bioinformatics findings. This study underscores the role of OS in IIM pathogenesis and identifies CDKN1A and CAMK2G as potential diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets. Key Points • Based on oxidative stress-related genes, we delineated two distinct OS-related subtypes in IIM, which exhibited significant biological and immunological differences. • Oxidative stress serves as a critical non-immune pathological driver in IIM progression.

papers.title: A synthetic peptide designed based on residues from a putative discontinuous epitope of crotoxin induces antibodies that partially reduce Crotalus durissus terrificus venom activity.
papers.authors: Sombrio EM, Freitas VG, da Silva Abel J, Cruz LA, Borghezan LA, de Sousa Anastácio R, Luiz GP, De-Pieri E, de Melo Cardoso M, Scussel R, Chávez-Olórtegui C, Fagundes MÍ, Machado-de-Ávila RA.
papers.abstract: Snakebites are a public health problem recognized by the World Health Organization as a neglected tropical disease. In Brazil, crotalic venom is considered the most toxic, with a complex composition of bioactive molecules, of which crotoxin (CTX) is the main component. The recommended treatment for snakebite is the use of commercial antivenom produced by hyper-immunizing horses, raising ethical concerns due to repeated venom inoculations that compromise animal welfare and lifespan. This study aimed to design and evaluate a bioinformatically derived peptide (PEP-CTX), corresponding to a putative discontinuous epitope of crotoxin, as an immunogen capable of inducing functional antibodies. Using bioinformatics tools, the peptide PEP-CTX was designed and synthesized by the FMOC Synthesis method. Mice were immunized and at the end of the immunizations, blood was collected, and the immunogenic effect of the peptide was evaluated by ELISA. To evaluate the effects of the serum, produced by PEP-CTX, a venom-induced cytotoxicity assay, and an assessment of phospholipase A2 (PLA2) activity were executed. PEP-CTX induced humoral immune response, generating antibodies that recognized both the PEP-CTX and Crotalus durissus terrificus crude venom. In addition, anti-PEP-CTX serum partially reduced the venom PLA2 activity halo and partially reduced venom-induced cytotoxicity under the experimental conditions evaluated, preserving cell viability, whereas venom incubated with PBS reduced cell viability to approximately 65% of the untreated control. These findings demonstrate that PEP-CTX, designed based on residues from a putative discontinuous epitope of CTX, can induce functionally active antibodies and support the further exploration of epitope-based immunogens as complementary tools for antivenom development.
papers.venue: Toxicon : official journal of the International Society on Toxinology

papers.title: Prognostic Modeling of Lysosomal Cell Death Signatures in Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Machine Learning Framework for Survival Outcome Prediction.
papers.authors: Wang R, Zhao Q, Liu S, Kong L, Ren D, Yan J, Yang S, Duan G.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. This study provides a comprehensive characterization of the transcriptomic landscape, cellular composition, and immune architecture of lung adenocarcinoma using multiomics approaches. Gene expression data were obtained from GEO (GSE131907) and TCGA-LUAD (n = 526). LRCD gene sets were curated from GeneCards, MSigDB, and published literature. Analyses included differential expression profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE131907, n = 11,376 cells), GSEA, and cell-cell communication mapping. A LASSO-based prognostic model with 10-fold cross-validation was built and validated across three independent cohorts using ROC and Kaplan-Meier analyses. Fourteen prognostically relevant genes were identified, including protective factors (BTK, CLNK, CTSG; HR 1). Single-cell analysis profiled 11,376 cells from one primary tumor and one normal lung sample. The prognostic model achieved moderate-to-good discrimination (AUC : 0.545-0.692) and effectively stratified patients by risk. Model genes correlated significantly with immune cell infiltration and checkpoint expression across risk groups, and functional enrichment highlighted immune trafficking, cytokine signaling, and cell adhesion pathways. This multiomics study identifies reliable LRCD-based prognostic markers and offers mechanistic insights into lung adenocarcinoma biology, with potential utility for clinical risk stratification.

papers.title: Mitochondrial Apoptosis-Related Genes Associated with Lung Cancer Progression and Prognosis: An Integrated Bioinformatics Analysis.
papers.authors: Wang J, Liu X, Wang X, Yang C.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, with mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) remodeling contributing to tumor progression and therapeutic resistance. This study aimed to identify clinically relevant mitochondrial OXPHOS-associated biomarkers and evaluate their biological, immunological, and prognostic significance in non-small cell lung cancer. Publicly available transcriptomic, genomic, and clinical datasets were integrated to identify differentially expressed OXPHOS-related genes in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC). Functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction, gene co-expression, pathway, immune infiltration, mutation, expression, and survival analyses were performed using established bioinformatics approaches. An eight-gene mitochondrial OXPHOS-centered network comprising COX6B1, COX5B, NDUFS8, NDUFB10, NDUFA12, NDUFB11, ECSIT, and TXN2 was identified. These genes were primarily associated with respiratory electron transport, oxidative phosphorylation, ATP metabolism, mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes, and electron transfer. Immune analyses revealed associations between OXPHOS alterations and immune-cell infiltration in LUAD and LUSC. Elevated expressions of COX6B1, COX5B, NDUFS8, NDUFA12, NDUFB11, and ECSIT was associated with poorer overall survival, whereas TXN2 showed no significant prognostic association. These findings identify a mitochondrial OXPHOS-related gene signature with potential prognostic and therapeutic relevance in lung cancer.

papers.title: Mitochondrial Metabolism-Related Candidate Signatures in Calcific Aortic Valve Disease Spectrum: An Exploratory Integrative Bioinformatics Study.
papers.authors: Yang M, Gui Y, Qian H, Zhang D.
papers.abstract: ​Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a progressive valvular disorder in which the role of mitochondrial metabolism remains incompletely understood. This exploratory study aimed to identify mitochondrial metabolism-related genes (MIMMRGs) associated with CAVD-spectrum valve remodeling. GSE83453 was used as the training dataset, and GSE51472 was used for expression-direction validation. Both datasets contain biologically and phenotypically heterogeneous groups of diseased valves. CAVD-associated differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were integrated with MIMMRGs, followed by functional enrichment analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and support vector machine-recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), expression validation, immune infiltration analysis, transcription factor analysis, drug and compound prediction, and molecular docking. A total of 909 DEGs and 1,234 MIMMRGs were identified, yielding 67 candidate genes enriched in metabolic and biosynthetic processes. ACADL and TDO2 were identified as candidate biomarkers and exhibited consistent expression differences between CAVD and normal samples in both datasets. Gene set enrichment analysis indicated the involvement of chemokine-related and immune-regulatory pathways. Four immune cell types differed between the CAVD and normal groups, and ACADL and TDO2 exhibited opposite correlations with naive B cells. HNF4A, STAT3, and AR were predicted to be common transcriptional regulators. Molecular docking indicated favorable in silico interactions between doxorubicin and ACADL and between dexamethasone and TDO2. In conclusion, ACADL and TDO2 are candidate biomarkers associated with mitochondrial metabolism and immune-related processes in heterogeneous CAVD-spectrum valve lesions. These findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and require independent clinical and experimental validation.

papers.title: The Interleukin-33/Growth Stimulation Expressed Gene 2 Signaling Axis in Transplantation: Context-Dependent Roles and Clinical Implications.
papers.authors: Ying H, Feng S, Jiang H.
papers.abstract: This article comprehensively summarizes the expression, mechanisms of action, and clinical significance of the IL-33/ST2 axis in solid organ transplantation and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Rather than being uniformly protective or pathogenic, the IL-33/ST2 axis exerts context-dependent effects: ST2L, expressed on regulatory T cells, group 2 innate lymphoid cells, and Th2 cells, promotes immune tolerance, whereas sST2 acts as a decoy receptor that blocks this pathway and promotes inflammation and fibrosis. The net effect depends on tissue-specific innate immune cell composition, differential ST2 isoform expression, donor versus recipient compartment, intervention timing and dosage, and the degree of ischemia-reperfusion injury. Clinically, elevated sST2 is associated with antibody-mediated rejection in kidney transplantation, graft dysfunction in heart transplantation, and treatment-refractory graft-versus-host disease in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. However, these are primarily observational associations; direct causal evidence from genetic or pharmacological intervention studies remains limited and is often derived from animal models. Comparative analysis across transplant types reveals that sST2 may complement established biomarkers such as donor-derived cell-free DNA and donor-specific antibodies, particularly for chronic graft fibrosis and DSA-negative rejection. Future research should use single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize the dynamic expression of ST2 isoforms across immune cells and transplant stages, and explore strategies to induce immune tolerance targeting the IL-33/ST2 axis to improve long-term outcomes for transplant patients.

papers.title: Computational image features of immune architecture reveal molecular patterns associated with outcome and risk of recurrence in microsatellite-stable or MSI-low colon cancers.
papers.authors: Song B, Maurya H, Khalighi S, Aqeel A, Corredor G, Hammouda K, Ozyoruk KB, Pathak T, Toro P, Chen C, Fu P, Zhao K, Lu C, Wang X, Willis J, Madabhushi A.
papers.abstract: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) density provides prognostic information in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD), but the additional value of TIL spatial organization remains unclear. We developed CoATIL, a computational pathology framework quantifying TIL spatial architecture from routine H&E-stained whole-slide images. The study included 461 patients with microsatellite-stable or MSI-low COAD. The model was trained using 140 patients from University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center, validated internally in 52 patients, and externally in The Cancer Genome Atlas (n = 130), and Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital (n = 139). Prognostic performance was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. CoATIL was compared with a clinical model and eight foundation-model-based multiple-instance learning approaches. CoATIL was associated with progression-free survival (HR per standard-deviation increase, 1.32; 95% CI 1.13-1.55; p < 0.001; C-index=0.66) and remained prognostic after adjustment for clinicopathologic factors in each validation cohort (adjusted HRs, 2.00-4.40; all p < 0.05). High-versus-low-risk stratification was retained within stage II (HR 3.07; 95% CI 1.83-5.15; p < 0.001) and stage III disease (HR 3.24; 95% CI 1.28-8.19; p = 0.013). The combined clinical-CoATIL model achieved a higher C-index than the clinical model alone (0.69 versus 0.61; paired bootstrap difference, 0.08; 95% CI 0.03-0.14). Exploratory genomic analyses associated AMER1 and FBXW7 mutations with lower and higher CoATIL risk scores, respectively. Spatial immune architecture extracted from routine histology provides complementary prognostic information in COAD. Prospective validation is warranted.

papers.title: Establishment of K562 cell lines expressing platelet antigen HPA-15 using lentiviral infection method.
papers.authors: Shen TC, Gao M, Wang FQ, Bian MY, Chen YP, Wang BQ.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to establish stable K562 cell lines individually overexpressing the HPA-15a and HPA-15b alloantigens for subsequent antigenic functional verification. A three-plasmid lentiviral system, including CD109 (HPA-15)-GFP, psPAX2, and pMD2.G, was transfected into HEK293T cells to produce lentivirus. K562 cells were infected with the harvested virus, followed by puromycin screening and single-cell cloning. Flow cytometry and Western blot were then performed to identify CD109 expression in cell clones. After blocking IgG Fc receptors on the cell surface, samples with confirmed HPA-15 positive and negative reactivity were applied to characterize the HPA-15 antigen reactivity of established cell clones using a cell-lysis-free MAIPA assay. Lentiviral packaging in HEK293T cells was verified by GFP fluorescence observation and RT-PCR detection. K562 cell lines stably overexpressing HPA-15a and HPA-15b were successfully generated. Repeated lentiviral infection significantly upregulated HPA-15 expression, with the final expression level approximately 12-fold higher than that in pooled platelets from 10 donors. A strong linear correlation was observed between positive sample volume and MAIPA assay signal intensity. Besides, the assay signals induced by positive samples were markedly higher than those of negative controls, confirming the HPA-15 antigen reactivity of recombinant cell lines. Stable K562 cell lines individually overexpressing HPA-15a and HPA-15b were successfully constructed. Meanwhile, an optimized cell-lysis-free MAIPA detection system based on IgG Fc receptor pre-blocking, which enabled semi-quantitative detection of HPA-15 alloantibodies, was developed.
papers.venue: Transfusion and apheresis science : official journal of the World Apheresis Association : official journal of the European Society for Haemapheresis

papers.title: Extracellular vesicles repair alveolar bone defect in periodontitis via FTH1 delivery to suppress ferroptosis and restore Th17/Treg balance.
papers.authors: Zhang Q, Ding Y, Liu X, Yang Y, Jiao Y, Liu L, Liu Y, Liu Z.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis involves an imbalanced immune microenvironment, characterized by an increased Th17/Treg ratio and iron overload-associated ferroptosis, which hinder alveolar bone repair. Although aggregate-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) from mesenchymal stem cells have been shown to modulate the Th17/Treg balance in periodontal tissues and to be more potent than single-cell-derived EVs in regulating CD4⁺ T cell differentiation, the underlying mechanisms remain largely unclear. To address this, we compared the protein cargo of EVs from stem cells from human exfoliated deciduous teeth and umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells cultured as aggregates or single cells. Our results suggest that aggregate culture may upregulate ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1) in EVs derived from MSCs of both ectodermal and mesodermal origins. FTH1 promoted collagen synthesis within aggregates and increased the yield of aggregate-derived EVs. Under inflammatory conditions, EV-delivered FTH1 maintained glutathione peroxidase 4 levels in T cells and reduced lipid peroxidation, suppressing ferroptosis and rebalancing Th17/Treg differentiation. Furthermore, in a rat periodontitis model, FTH1 was required for EVs to restore the Th17/Treg balance and promote alveolar bone repair. These findings suggest that the EV-FTH1-ferroptosis pathway could serve as a novel target for periodontal immunotherapy.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics identifies tumor-intrinsic and stromal programs associated with immune exclusion in NSCLC.
papers.authors: Guegan JP, Bonhomme B, Peyraud F, Rey C, Cousin S, Aldea M, Barlesi F, Besse B, Planchard D, Karpinich N, Kim J, Cheikh R, Yadavilli S, Bessede A, Italiano A.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has reshaped the treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet durable benefit remains limited to a subset of patients. One major pattern of resistance is immune exclusion, in which CD8+ T cells accumulate in stromal regions but fail to penetrate tumor nests. Here, using discovery and non-overlapping internal validation cohorts of ICB-treated NSCLC patients, we show that spatial CD8+ T-cell exclusion is associated with lower objective response rates and shorter progression-free survival. To characterize the molecular programs linked to this phenotype, we integrated GeoMx spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic profiling, TCR-probe expression analysis, multiplex immunohistofluorescence, and single-cell spatial neighborhood analyses. Compared with infiltrated tumors, immune-excluded tumors showed reduced expression of genes encoding antigen-presentation machinery in the tumor compartment, including HLA class I genes and TAP1, with an altered relationship between IFN-γ-associated transcriptional signals and expression of antigen-presentation machinery. At the stromal level, excluded tumors were enriched for myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblast programs and peri-epithelial collagen-rich architecture, whereas infiltrated tumors displayed immune-supportive stromal signatures. CD8-enriched regions from excluded tumors showed reduced metabolic activation and lower TCR-probe expression diversity, without a marked increase in canonical exhaustion markers. These findings provide an integrated, compartment-resolved description of tumor-intrinsic and stromal features associated with immune exclusion in NSCLC and support further evaluation of spatial immune contexture as a complementary biomarker in ICB-treated patients.

papers.title: The Role of NK‑Cell Dysregulation in Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Rheumatic Immune Diseases: Mechanisms and Translational Advances.
papers.authors: Zhu L, Hua L, Du H.
papers.abstract: Rheumatic autoimmune diseases induce sustained systemic inflammatory imbalance and substantially elevate the incidence of adverse pregnancy complications, such as recurrent spontaneous abortion, preeclampsia, preterm delivery, and fetal growth restriction. Decidual natural killer (dNK) cells constitute the major lymphocyte subset at the maternal-fetal interface and maintain the homeostasis of immune tolerance, trophoblast invasion and spiral artery remodeling; peripheral NK (pNK) cells differ greatly from dNK cells in phenotype, cytotoxicity and secretory function under the regulation of local uterine microenvironment. Emerging evidence indicates that dysregulated NK‑cell number, subset distribution, receptor signalling and cytokine release may perturb the decidual immune‑vascular microenvironment and contribute to inflammatory placental‑associated pathology, with considerably more robust mechanistic support in antiphospholipid syndrome than in systemic lupus erythematosus, primary Sjögren's syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, and systemic sclerosis. Solid preclinical and clinical evidence confirms that excessive NK cell activation participates in placental injury in antiphospholipid syndrome, whereas the direct inflammatory pathogenic cascades underlying gestational complications remain insufficiently clarified for other rheumatic disorders. This work elucidates the physiological heterogeneity of pNK and dNK cells, delineates six core inflammatory axes driving NK-mediated placental injury, characterizes disease-specific aberrant inflammatory phenotypes of NK cells, summarizes translational advances in NK-targeted anti-inflammatory strategies, and identifies existing research bottlenecks. We also put forward prospective research schemes based on single-cell multi-omics and large-scale clinical cohorts to reveal NK-centered inflammatory pathology, which offers theoretical support for immune inflammation regulation in childbearing-age women with rheumatic autoimmune diseases.

papers.title: Neutrophil fate in bone infection: Mechanisms, microenvironment, and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.authors: Cai C, Ji Y, Mei J, Wang Z, Liu Q, Fan W, Zhao Y, Chen X, Zhu C, Zhu W, Li Q.
papers.abstract: The clinical challenge of eradicating bone infection stems from microbial persistence within a distinct skeletal niche that is poorly perfused, hypoxic, mineralised, and highly susceptible to collateral damage. Neutrophils are central arbiters of this process and function as a double-edged sword: they are indispensable for initial pathogen containment, yet can become major drivers of chronic osteolysis, biofilm persistence, and inflammation when their effector programmes turn maladaptive. Recent high-resolution single-cell and spatial analyses have overturned the traditional view of neutrophils as short-lived, homogeneous cells, instead revealing a complex spectrum of functional states shaped by the infected bone microenvironment. In this Review, we use a neutrophil fate framework that distinguishes three related but non-equivalent levels: irreversible terminal fates, non-terminal tissue-disposition states and outcomes, and upstream fate-biasing states or processes. Terminal fates include apoptosis with subsequent efferocytic clearance, suicidal NETosis, pyroptosis, necroptosis, ferroptosis, mitochondrial permeability transition-driven necrosis, and secondary necrosis. By contrast, non-lytic (vital) NET release is considered an effector process rather than a terminal fate. Reverse migration is treated as a non-terminal tissue-exit outcome, whereas inflammatory retention is considered a non-terminal persistence state. Upstream fate-biasing factors include phenotypic or activation states, such as cellular ageing, NET-prone activation, and apoptosis delay, as well as regulatory processes including autophagy and metabolic or redox stress; none of these is classified as an independent terminal fate. We further examine how these terminal fates, non-terminal tissue-disposition states and outcomes, and upstream fate-biasing states and processes are spatially organised across osteomyelitic lesions and biofilm-associated interfaces, and how they govern interactions with osteoblasts, osteoclasts, and macrophages to determine the balance between antimicrobial control and progressive skeletal destruction. We also discuss emerging therapeutic paradigms aimed not at broadly suppressing neutrophil recruitment, but at precisely redirecting neutrophil fate, thereby providing a conceptual basis for stage-specific immunomodulation in orthopaedic infection. The Translational Potential of this Article This Review provides a fate-based framework for understanding how neutrophils shape the balance between pathogen control, biofilm persistence, osteolysis, and tissue repair in orthopaedic infection. By linking neutrophil fate programmes to distinct lesion microenvironments, including osteomyelitic lesions, implant-associated biofilms, contiguous soft-tissue infection, and fracture-related infection, this article highlights potential translational opportunities for stage- and compartment-specific immune modulation. These include improving patient stratification, guiding the timing of surgical source control and implant retention or removal, optimising dead-space management and local antimicrobial delivery, supporting vascularised soft-tissue reconstruction, and developing biomarkers that distinguish protective antimicrobial neutrophil responses from destructive inflammatory persistence. This framework may help shift future orthopaedic infection management from nonspecific suppression of inflammation toward precision redirection of maladaptive neutrophil fate while preserving early host defence and tissue repair capacity.

papers.title: A multi-omics computational framework identifies cell-type-specific therapeutic targets and active compounds of Tripterygium wilfordii Hook.f. against diabetic kidney disease.
papers.authors: Wu R, Wu R, Gandotra S, Lv L, Lee B, He Y.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of chronic and end-stage kidney disease, and current therapies leave patients at high risk. Tripterygium wilfordii Hook.f. (TWHF), a traditional Chinese medicine, reduces proteinuria in DKD, but the compounds and molecular targets responsible remain poorly defined. We hypothesized that specific bioactive compounds of TWHF ameliorate DKD through interactions with cell-type-specific molecular targets, thereby modulating inflammatory, immune, and tissue-remodeling pathways involved in disease progression. By integrating transcriptomic analysis, immune-infiltration profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing, virtual gene knockout analysis, and molecular docking, this study developed a comprehensive computational framework to investigate the cell-type-specific and multi-target mechanisms of TWHF in DKD. Using the GEO study GSE30529 (with 22 microdissected human kidney samples), we intersected predicted TWHF targets with DKD-associated and differentially expressed genes from human kidney tubules, and identified four key genes (CCR2, MMP7, PLK2, and PSMB9) that were upregulated in DKD and negatively correlated with glomerular filtration rate. The immune microenvironment in diseased kidneys was found to be remodelled based on an immune-infiltration analysis. Single-cell analysis localized MMP7 to loop-of-Henle epithelial cells, CCR2 to leukocyte, and PLK2 and PSMB9 to endothelial cells, and these genes were implicated in epithelial remodeling and endothelial dysfunction based on virtual gene knockout analysis. Furthermore, molecular docking predicted interactions between the four key proteins and three hub TWHF compounds, with triptolide showing the strongest predicted affinity. In an independent triptolide-response dataset generated from A549 cells, triptolide produced a dose- and time-dependent reduction in PLK2 expression. Collectively, CCR2, MMP7, PLK2, and PSMB9 were identified to be candidate therapeutic targets and Triptolide as a leading active compound, with the potential triptolide-PLK2 regulatory relationship should be further investigated. These results support our hypothesis that TWHF acts through direct, multi-compound engagement of multiple cell-type-specific targets, pointing to a multi-target, multi-pathway mechanism for TWHF in DKD and providing a mechanistic framework for subsequent experimental validation.

papers.title: Identification of mitophagy-related genes with diagnostic value in focal segmental glomerulosclerosis using bioinformatics analysis.
papers.authors: Ma J, Ma T, Zhang Y, Wei H.
papers.abstract: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), a major cause of end-stage renal disease, involves podocyte injury and immune dysregulation. We integrated GEO transcriptomic datasets to identify 839 differentially expressed genes and 33 differential mitophagy-related genes via differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Machine learning identified six candidate diagnostic biomarkers, SLIRP, BLVRB, ATP6V1F, COX5B, TMEM14A, and TRMT112, with moderate-to-good discriminatory capacity across cohorts. xCell analysis revealed extensive renal immune remodeling in FSGS with expanded pro-inflammatory cells, diminished naive T cells and Tregs, and tight correlations between hub genes and immune profiles. Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis suggested a trend of downregulation of hub genes in FSGS podocytes, alongside suppressed transcriptomic signatures of mitochondrial energy metabolism and mitophagy-related pathways. qRT-PCR and western blot validated their downregulation at the whole-renal-tissue level in FSGS mouse models. These six genes may serve as diagnostic candidates and provide research clues for exploring mitophagy mechanisms in FSGS.

papers.title: Microbial dynamics across commercial spaceflights of varying duration.
papers.authors: Krishnavajhala A, Gingras MC, Santiago-Rodriguez TM, Chen Y, Bandaranaike D, Bhamidipati S, Qin X, Kottapalli K, Momin Z, Santhanam A, Walker K, Wang Q, Griffin SM, Masternak MM, Ross MC, Muzny D, Wu J, Urquieta E, Gibbs RA, Doddapaneni H.
papers.abstract: Spaceflight introduces environmental stressors that can alter human microbiomes and immune responses. We analyzed 259 and 17 biospecimens for microbiome and single-cell studies from n = 6 astronauts across two commercial International Space Station (ISS) missions: Axiom 2 (10-day mission) and Axiom 3 (21-day mission). Samples included saliva, stool, urine, and body swabs from 10 anatomical sites, profiled via 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene amplicon sequencing. Gut and oral microbiomes remained stable, while skin-associated communities exhibited transient diversity shifts post-flight. Taxonomic analysis revealed individual and site-specific patterns, as well as from the spaceflight/ISS environment. Cytokine profiling from single-cell data indicated immune activation, with IL-32 and IL-16 transcripts elevated in Axiom 2 and Axiom 3. Microbiome and interleukin correlation analyses found 14 significant associations in Axiom 2 data. These findings provide an integrated view of microbiome individuality. Our study represents a descriptive comparison of two missions, informing strategies for crew health on future long-duration missions.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptome atlas revealed liver immune features in biliary atresia.
papers.authors: Liu X, Liu Z, Wang H, Chen Y, Ye M, Li X, Geng Y, Cui X, He F.
papers.abstract: Background While immune dysfunction is recognized as pivotal in biliary atresia (BA) pathogenesis, comprehensive characterization of disease-specific immune cell subtypes and stromal components remains incomplete. This study aims to define the altered hepatic immune-stromal landscape and aberrant intercellular communication networks associated with BA progression using single-cell transcriptomics. Methods We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on BA liver tissues to profile immune and stromal cell populations. Cellular subclustering, differential gene expression, pathway enrichment, and cell-cell communication analyses were employed to identify potential pathogenic drivers and predicted possible signaling networks. Multiplex immunofluorescence staining was used to verify receptor-ligand interaction in BA liver. Results BA livers exhibited profound expansion of pro-inflammatory neutrophil subsets - Neutrophils with interferon-stimulated genes (Neu_ISG), Aged neutrophils (Neu_Aged) - with transcriptional signatures suggestive of enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, extracellular matrix (ECM) modulation, and cytokine activity. Concurrent cytotoxic/immunoregulatory lymphocyte populations - Effector memory CD4⁺ T Cell (CD4⁺ TEM), Tregs, cytotoxic NK cells- showed upregulated inflammatory and oxidative stress pathways. Periportal and lymphatic liver endothelial cells (LECs) demonstrated significant perturbations. Central venous LECs displayed signatures of oxidative stress and dysregulated proliferation/migration. Cell-cell communication analysis highlighted a possibly dominant "CXCL12-CXCR4" axis mediating neutrophil recruitment across endothelia, NK&T/B, and myeloid cells. Enhanced "MIF-CD74/CXCR4" signaling between endothelia and immune cells, "VEGFB-VEGFR1" interactions between hepatocyte-cholangiocyte compartments and central venous/periportal endothelia were observed, suggesting that these interactions are associated with BA progression. Conclusion Our scRNA-seq atlas uncovers coordinated innate/adaptive immune responses and endothelial-stromal dysfunction that shape a hepatic niche in BA associated with ROS, unchecked inflammation, and fibrotic remodeling. Key cellular and molecular contributors include pathogenic neutrophils, cytotoxic lymphocytes, and injured endothelia, which interact via "CXCL12-CXCR4" and "VEGFB-VEGFR1" signaling axes. These findings from the present exploratory study point to potential novel therapeutic targets (e.g., neutrophil subsets, chemokine pathways) for mitigating BA pathogenesis.

papers.title: Systemic immune dysregulation and local barrier failure as predictors of septic shock in acute appendicitis: a large-scale multicenter interpretable machine learning study.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Rui Y.
papers.abstract: Background The transition from localized acute appendicitis to systemic septic shock is driven by complex immune and metabolic dysregulation combined with anatomical barrier failure. Accurately predicting early hemodynamic deterioration remains clinically challenging. This study aimed to develop an interpretable multimodal machine learning model by integrating systemic immunological profiles with local sonographic characteristics. Methods This multicenter cohort study included 3000 patients with acute appendicitis. Following rigorous data reduction using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, eight supervised machine learning algorithms were constructed. The optimal predictive algorithm was comprehensively evaluated across training, internal testing, and independent external validation cohorts. The SHapley Additive exPlanations framework was utilized to provide transparent model interpretability, and the final algorithm was deployed as a dynamic digital calculator. Results Six independent predictors were identified, including the Systemic Immune Inflammation Index, C-reactive protein to albumin ratio, glucose to lymphocyte ratio, Prognostic Nutritional Index, periappendiceal fluid, and the sonographic loss of the submucosal echogenic layer. The Random Forest model demonstrated the highest discriminative performance among the evaluated algorithms, achieving an area under the curve of 0.914. The model's discrimination, calibration, and decision-analytic performance were consistently evaluated in the internal testing and external validation cohorts. SHAP analysis indicated that systemic inflammatory indices and sonographic features reflecting local disease severity made important contributions to the model's predicted risk of septic shock. These findings should be interpreted as predictive associations rather than evidence of biological causality or synergy. Conclusion This multicenter study developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for early risk stratification of septic shock. The publicly accessible calculator may support individualized risk assessment; however, prospective impact evaluation is required to determine whether its clinical implementation facilitates earlier resuscitation or improves patient outcomes.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

papers.title: Immune microenvironment in rotator cuff healing: from macrophage dynamics to immunomodulatory regenerative therapies.
papers.authors: Li F, Fu Z, Zhang X, Ke X, Gao X.
papers.abstract: Rotator cuff repair is increasingly limited by biology rather than fixation alone: the repaired tendon commonly heals through fibrovascular scar rather than recreating the graded tendon-fibrocartilage-bone enthesis, particularly in aging, metabolic disease, muscle degeneration, and poor bone quality. The immune microenvironment is a dynamic determinant of whether injury progresses toward persistent inflammation and fibrosis or toward resolution and regeneration. This Review synthesizes immune regulation across the rotator cuff muscle-tendon-enthesis-bone unit, with emphasis on macrophage heterogeneity, efferocytosis, autophagy, immunometabolism, mechanosensing, and immune-stromal crosstalk. Human single-cell studies identify pro-fibrotic macrophage, senescent tenocyte, osteopontin/TGF-beta, and endothelial programs in rotator cuff scar, while mechanistic studies nominate resolution pathways as therapeutic targets. We critically evaluate cytokine/chemokine modulation, extracellular vesicles, senomorphic strategies, bioactive ions, ROS-responsive materials, nanoengineered interfaces, and rehabilitation-based immunomodulation. Across these approaches, the key translational requirements are causal mechanism, validation in chronic or aged disease models and human tissue, integration of structural and mechanical outcomes, arthroscopic deployability, manufacturing feasibility, and biomarker-guided patient selection. Together, these data support a shift from nonspecific anti-inflammatory augmentation toward mechanism-based, pro-resolution strategies for durable tendon-to-bone repair.

papers.title: Association of CDKN2A overexpression with poor prognosis, radioresistance, and immunosuppression in colorectal cancer.
papers.authors: Lin Y, Wang Z, Ju G, Zhang Y, Huang Z, Liu S, Xu B, Zhan Z.
papers.abstract: Background In colorectal cancer (CRC), dysregulated cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 2A (CDKN2A) contributes to disease progression. This investigation sought to explore the link between CDKN2A expression and the effectiveness of radiotherapy in CRC, and to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Methods Transcriptomic and clinical datasets were procured from the Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus databases. Immune cell infiltration was assessed using xCell, CIBERSORT, and EPIC methods. Biological mechanisms were investigated through the utilization of Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes. HCT 116 cells were used for in vitro and in vivo experiments. Results Bulk and single-cell transcriptome analyses and immunohistochemistry consistently revealed elevated CDKN2A expression in tumor specimens from patients with CRC. Patients with tumors that were nonresponsive to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy had significantly higher CDKN2A expression than those of responders ( P = 0.039). CDKN2A knockdown in tumor led to a marked decrease in the proliferation, invasion, and migration capabilities, and this effect was enhanced by combined X-ray irradiation. Elevated CDKN2A expression was linked to markedly worse survival. In the tumor immune microenvironment, CDKN2A expression was negatively linked to CD8 + cell infiltration and positively correlated with the levels of immunosuppressive factors. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that elevated CDKN2A expression is linked to transcriptional regulation, amino acid metabolism, protein folding, and the TGF-β signaling pathway. Conclusion In CRC, CDKN2A overexpression is associated with unfavorable responses to radiotherapy, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and poor prognosis. Suppression of CDKN2A expression could potentially improve therapeutic outcomes in CRC patients. More experimental and clinical studies are still needed to verify and further distinguish the similarities and differences between colon cancer and rectal cancer.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: An m 5 C-associated NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF programme marks melanoma cell states and immune features.
papers.authors: Liu A, Yuan K, Yi S, Mao H, Xie X, Yin S, Fan H, Zhang A, Liu X, Hu Y, Xu A, Chen W, He Y.
papers.abstract: Background RNA 5-methylcytosine (m 5 C)-associated programmes may help characterise melanoma cell states and their immune context. We investigated an NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF (NYC) programme using patient-matched sequencing, experimental perturbation and multiscale transcriptomic analyses. Methods We analysed m 5 C-MeRIP-seq and matched Input RNA data from three melanoma-adjacent-normal patient pairs, using a paired edgeR interaction model for regional IP enrichment. Tissue and cell experiments included NSUN5 knockdown, CENPF-targeted MeRIP-qPCR and western blotting. Clinical analyses considered proliferation and sampling site. Trajectory and regulatory inference were restricted to malignant cells from GSE215120, with patient-level summaries. Treatment-associated changes were examined in 43 paired patients from GSE91061. Computational perturbation and transcriptomic signature reversal prioritised candidate regulators and compounds. Results Two CENPF regions showed increased relative IP enrichment after Input adjustment (4.97- and 5.85-fold; BH q = 0.0457 and 0.0074). NSUN5 knockdown reduced CENPF m 5 C enrichment and protein abundance. NYC was associated with proliferation; its survival association did not persist after proliferation adjustment. Within malignant cells, NYC-High retained an association with an immune-resistance expression programme after G2M/E2F and depth adjustment (nine patients; BH q = 0.0156). Regulatory analyses prioritised MLX, whose simulated knockout and overexpression produced opposing reference-flow alignments (BH q = 0.0134 and 0.0201). MLX regulon activity was associated with glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation after adjustment. In GSE91061, responders showed a greater treatment-associated NYC decrease than non-responders (mean change difference -0.209; permutation P = 0.0138). Drug screening generated candidates for experimental testing. Conclusions NYC provides an m 5 C-associated framework connecting patient-derived molecular observations to malignant-cell states and immune features. YBX1 remains a candidate reader, and regulatory, treatment-associated and drug-prioritisation findings do not establish a complete causal pathway or a clinically validated predictive biomarker.

papers.title: Joint disease in systemic lupus erythematosus: clinical manifestations, immunopathology, and treatment.
papers.authors: Ong M, Tariq F, Mahto A, Wincup C.
papers.abstract: Joint involvement affects the majority of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and is consistently ranked among the manifestations with the largest impact on daily function, yet lupus synovium remains one of the least interrogated major target tissues in this disease. The primary literature on lupus synovial tissue rests mainly on two datasets, neither generated by single-cell transcriptomic or mass cytometric methods, and what they describe is a relatively pauci-immune and myeloid-dominated compartment carrying an interferon-inducible transcriptional signature in situ, without the ectopic germinal centers and expanded pathogenic fibroblast populations that characterize rheumatoid synovitis. The cell populations now central to systemic lupus biology, among them T peripheral helper cells and double-negative 2 B cells, have never been examined in lupus synovial tissue, so that every cellular account of this compartment remains an extrapolation from rheumatoid arthritis. Recent large-cohort data nevertheless indicate that lupus arthropathy is not a single entity, since non-deforming arthritis and Jaccoud's arthropathy are both associated with a high type I interferon signature whereas arthritis with clinically irreducible deformity is interferon-low, although whether these represent distinct biological trajectories or successive stages of a single process remains to be established. This heterogeneity is invisible to the instruments used in practice, because the composite indices that grade disease activity and determine eligibility for advanced therapy depend on the detection of joint swelling at the bedside, while musculoskeletal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging independently demonstrate inflammation in approximately half of patients whose joints appear clinically unremarkable, together with erosive change in patients who lack anti-citrullinated protein antibodies. Misclassification of articular disease is therefore systematic and bidirectional, and the same failure has propagated into drug development, where no recent registrational program has used imaging to define articular response, even though the proportion of patients failing on articular endpoints lies between roughly a third and a half. This review synthesizes the immunopathological, biomarker, imaging and therapeutic literatures, and argues that single-cell interrogation of the lupus synovium, a lupus-specific imaging scoring system and a validated imaging-anchored articular outcome measure are the necessary next steps if this manifestation is to be treated with the precision now applied to lupus nephritis.

papers.title: Pathology-guided multimodal transformer predicts postoperative survival benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy in glioma: from DNA damage repair to immune characterization.
papers.authors: Li Z, Duan X, Lian J, Li X, Liang Q, Liu X, Tan Y, Yang G, Du J, Wu L, Wang X, Zhang H.
papers.abstract: Introduction High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are aggressive primary brain tumors with high recurrence rates and poor prognosis. Survival benefit from adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) varies substantially across patients, and reliable preoperative biomarkers for treatment stratification remain limited. This study aims to develop an interpretable multimodal deep learning model integrating whole-slide histopathological images and multiparametric MRI to preoperatively predict survival benefit from adjuvant TMZ in HGG patients. Methods A Transformer-based multimodal fusion model was proposed. Key tumor regions were identified from whole-slide pathology images via weakly supervised clustering, and pathological features were extracted using attention-based multiple instance learning. Concurrently, 2.5D tumor subregional features were derived from multiparametric MRI sequences. These multimodal features were deeply fused using a Transformer encoder. The model was developed and validated on a multicenter cohort (504 patients), and its biological basis was explored through transcriptomic analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction networks, and immune deconvolution. Results The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.910, 0.861, and 0.833 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Transcriptomic analysis implicated DNA damage repair processes in high-benefit patients, suggesting that enhanced DNA repair capacity may contribute to TMZ sensitivity. Immune deconvolution showed higher M1 macrophage infiltration and lower regulatory T cell abundance in the high-benefit group, consistent with a less immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Importantly, low-benefit patients who completed TMZ chemotherapy had shorter survival than those treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy alone or surgery alone. Conclusion This model identifies patients unlikely to benefit from standard TMZ chemotherapy, providing a tool for postoperative personalized treatment stratification and optimization of therapeutic strategies in HGGs.

papers.title: Regulatory network remodeling and potential non-canonical associations of the transcription factor SP1 during inflammation-to-cancer transformation in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Du B, Zhang J, Liu H, Xing X, Wang X, Wang P.
papers.abstract: Background Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is closely linked to chronic inflammation, but the transcriptional mechanisms connecting epithelial inflammatory remodeling with malignant transformation remain incompletely understood. Methods We integrated secondary analysis of published single-cell epithelial transition-state data, virtual SP1 perturbation, TCGA analyses, xCell immune infiltration analysis, TIDE-based exploratory immunotherapy prediction, Co-IP/MS, and a 4NQO-induced mouse model to investigate SP1-associated network remodeling during ESCC carcinogenesis. Results SP1 regulatory importance increased across pairwise epithelial state comparisons. In adjacent normal epithelial cells, virtual SP1 overexpression affected genes linked to inflammatory response, NF-κB-related signaling, epithelial stress remodeling, and proliferation. SP1 expression correlated with immune infiltration features and immune checkpoint gene expression, and TIDE analysis suggested an association with predicted immunotherapy-related features. SP1-binding partners were enriched in RNA metabolism, RNA splicing, and nuclear protein-complex annotations, suggesting potential non-canonical regulatory associations that require further experimental validation. Conclusions SP1 may represent a progressively enhanced transcriptional hub during inflammation-associated ESCC carcinogenesis, with state-dependent network remodeling spanning epithelial inflammatory stress, malignant transformation, and tumor immune features.

papers.title: Addressing unmet clinical needs in treatment-resistant breast cancer: expanding the diagnostic-prognostic landscape through next-generation inflammatory signatures.
papers.authors: Obeagu EI.
papers.abstract: Treatment-resistant breast cancer remains a major clinical challenge because conventional clinicopathological and molecular biomarkers incompletely capture the dynamic interactions between tumour cells, immunity, inflammation, and the systemic host response. Next-generation inflammatory signatures offer an opportunity to expand the diagnostic-prognostic landscape by integrating cellular, molecular, immune, and thromboinflammatory indicators with established tumour characteristics. This narrative review critically examines emerging evidence for neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, C-reactive protein, cytokines, tumour-associated macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, neutrophil extracellular traps, coagulation biomarkers, and liquid-biopsy-derived measures in treatment-resistant breast cancer. Particular attention is given to sources of heterogeneity, including population characteristics, tumour subtype, treatment exposure, comorbid inflammation, sampling time, specimen processing, analytical platforms, and inconsistent biomarker thresholds. The review further evaluates the transition from biomarker discovery to clinical decision support, highlighting the need for prospective multicentre validation, standardised analytical procedures, external validation of computational models, and integration with molecular subtyping, circulating tumour DNA, imaging, and immune profiling. Rather than interpreting inflammation as a static prognostic variable, longitudinal inflammatory trajectories may provide earlier signals of biological treatment resistance and complement conventional measures of disease progression. Future research should establish clinically actionable inflammatory combinations and evaluate biomarker-guided anti-inflammatory strategies alongside standard therapies. Ultimately, integrating inflammatory phenotypes with tumour molecular characteristics may facilitate earlier recognition of resistance and more precise, dynamic, and equitable breast cancer management.

papers.title: Dietary exogenous microRNAs in the gut: biological effects, mechanistic evidence, and controversies.
papers.authors: Méndez-García A, García-Mendoza MA, Pérez-Martínez P, Figueroa-Ramírez M, Banerjee A, Pathak S, Duttaroy AK, Paul S.
papers.abstract: Dietary exogenous microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as potential mediators of interorganismal communication, with growing interest in their ability to influence gastrointestinal physiology and the gut microbiota. These molecules encompass plant-derived miRNAs implicated in cross-kingdom regulation, animal-derived dietary miRNAs involved in cross-species communication, and maternal milk miRNAs that may participate in mother-to-offspring molecular crosstalk. A proportion of dietary miRNAs are associated with extracellular vesicles or other protective complexes, which may enhance their stability during food processing and gastrointestinal transit and facilitate interactions with intestinal epithelial cells, immune cells, and microbial communities. This review critically evaluates recent computational, detection-based, in vitro, in vivo, and human observational evidence concerning the gastrointestinal stability, uptake, target engagement, and biological activity of dietary exogenous miRNAs. Experimental studies have reported effects on inflammatory signaling, epithelial barrier integrity, macrophage polarization, intestinal development, tumor-associated pathways, and gut microbial composition and gene expression. However, the strength of this evidence varies considerably. In particular, detection of dietary miRNAs in food, extracellular vesicles, feces, or recipient tissues does not by itself establish functional target regulation, while studies using purified vesicles, synthetic miRNA mimics, or engineered delivery systems may involve exposures that differ substantially from normal dietary intake. Moreover, biological effects observed following whole-vesicle administration cannot always be attributed specifically to their miRNA cargo. Collectively, current evidence provides stronger support for the biological plausibility of local gastrointestinal effects than for widespread systemic regulation after dietary exposure. Further studies using physiologically relevant doses, rigorous miRNA-specific loss-of-function approaches, direct target validation, standardized analytical methods, and controlled human interventions will be essential to establish the functional significance and translational potential of dietary exogenous miRNAs.
